pages.name: Adding and setting up the cards

DashboardWide.dc.html.title: Both cards on a wide dashboard

t-status.text: Status card: a new dashboard card that shows one 3D printer's stage, job, progress, layers left, time left, problems and temperatures, in every state from printing to offline.

n-main.text: Shows the new 3D printer status card on a phone dashboard, above a room card for context. The card shows the printer name, model and online dot, a stage chip with a quiet pulsing dot, a short note beside the chip only when it adds something (print speed, or since when it is paused), the job with its cover image, a big percentage, a progress bar drawn as 40 thin layer lines, layers left, time left and finish time, a problems panel or a quiet "No problems" line, and temperature tiles for each nozzle, the bed and the chamber with current, target and a heating, cooling or at-target mark. The H2D chamber tile shows its target; single-nozzle printers show one nozzle and no chamber. The offline stage is greyed and shows no live values. Try: tap the card header to see where it leads; tap the two top bar buttons; in the problem stage collapse the problems panel and tap "What this means"; in the choose stage pick a printer and press "Show this printer". Unbuilt: all of it, this is a new design. Tweaks: accent, motion (off also stops the pulsing dot), theme (dark or light), stage.

t-controls.text: Control card: a new dashboard card that gathers every control of one 3D printer into six tidy groups, with a confirmation before stopping a print.

n-controlsphone.text: Shows the new 3D printer controls card on a phone dashboard. One card per printer, with six collapsible groups: Print (Pause or Resume, and Stop, which always asks first), Speed (Silent, Standard, Sport, Ludicrous), Temperature (a stepper per nozzle, bed and chamber with the current reading and a heating, cooling or at target mark; the first raise from Off jumps to a usable target), Fans (slider plus switch each), Lights, and More (airduct mode, camera, prompt sound, silence buzzer, force refresh). Parts a printer lacks are left out: the single stage has no buzzer button, and rack buttons appear only on printers with a hotend rack, so neither sample shows them. Try: tap Stop and answer the sheet; raise the right nozzle target and watch the mark change; drag a fan to zero, then switch it back on. Unbuilt: all of it; this is a new card. Tweaks: accent, motion, theme (dark or light), stage.

t-adding.text: Adding and setting up the cards: both cards in the Add to dashboard dialog, and the card editors with a printer picker and switches for what to show.

n-addcardphone.text: Shows how the two new 3D printer cards are added and set up on a phone. The Add to dashboard dialog lists "3D printer status" and "3D printer controls" with picture-only previews drawn exactly like the cards on the other boards; its search has the pattern workbench beside it. Add opens the card editor: a short preview window that stays on top and moves to the part a setting changes, a printer picker listing only supported printers, and switches for what to show. With no supported printer, the editor says so, links to adding an integration and keeps Save off. Try: clear the search to see every card, or apply ^3d printer (status|controls)$ in the workbench. Add the status card, pick Office P1S, turn Chamber temperature off, then press Show all. In the control editor, hide groups, then press Stop in the preview. Unbuilt: all of it; both cards, the dialog entries and the editors are new. Tweaks: accent, motion, theme (dark or light), stage.

t-wide.text: Wide dashboard: the status and control cards for one printer side by side, with a second printer's status card in its own section below.

n-dashboardwide.text: Shows a wide dashboard with the Workshop H2D status and control cards side by side and the Office P1S status card in its own section below. The status card has a stage chip with a quiet pulsing dot, a big percentage, a bar of thin layer lines, time left, problems, and temperature tiles with current, target and a heating or cooling mark; the active nozzle stays marked while idle. The control card groups Print, Speed, Temperature, Fans, Lights and More in a grid that folds to one column at phone width. When the printer is offline every control is truly disabled and the reason stays readable. Try: press Pause then Resume and watch the status card follow, with focus staying on the button; press Stop and answer the confirmation; raise the left nozzle target or drag a fan slider. Unbuilt: all of it; both cards, the printer lookup by entity keys and the link between controls and status are new. Tweaks: accent, motion, theme (dark or light), stage.
